content:
Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also raising its prices. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the Apple TV monthly fee will increase from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

The Apple One Individual plan monthly fee will also be adjusted accordingly.

Apple TV and Apple One raise prices together

Below are the pricing details:

  • Apple TV (monthly): US$14.99 (originally US$12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): US$119 (originally US$99)
  • Apple One Individual plan: US$21.95 (originally US$19.95)

Other Apple One plan prices remain unchanged. When Apple raised the Apple Music monthly fee last month, it also raised the monthly fees for the Apple One Family plan and Apple One Premier plan, but did not adjust the Individual plan.

The new prices take effect today and apply to new subscribers. Apple says existing subscribers will receive notification approximately one month before the price increase.

Apple last raised the Apple TV monthly fee in August 2025, when it went from US$9.99 to US$12.99 per month. That price increase did not adjust the annual plan or Apple One bundle pricing.

Over the past year, Apple has significantly expanded Apple TV's content lineup. Last October, Apple announced a deal with Formula 1, becoming F1's exclusive broadcast partner in the United States. The F1 streaming service is included in the standard Apple TV subscription fee at no extra cost.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) streaming to Apple TV at no additional cost. Previously, MLS required a separate MLS Season Pass subscription to watch.

Apple has also had several well-received new productions in recent years, including the fourth season of "Ted Lasso." Today, Apple TV also premiered the second season of "Dark Matter." The sixth season of "Slow Horses" will debut on September 16.

What do you think of Apple TV's new pricing? Is US$14.99 good value? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
